📺 Good Girls (2018–2021)

Good Girls follows three suburban mothers, Beth Boland, Ruby Hill, and Annie Marks, who find themselves struggling with overwhelming financial and personal problems. Desperate to take control of their lives, the women decide to rob a local grocery store, believing the money will solve their difficulties. However, their seemingly simple plan takes a dangerous turn when they discover that the stolen money belongs to a criminal organization led by the mysterious and charismatic Rio. As the women become increasingly involved in money laundering and organized crime, they struggle to balance their secret criminal activities with motherhood, marriage, friendships, and everyday responsibilities. Their decisions lead to unexpected betrayals, dangerous encounters, and complicated moral dilemmas that constantly test their loyalty to one another. Starring Christina Hendricks, Retta, Mae Whitman, and Manny Montana, the series delivers gripping suspense, dark humor, and emotional storytelling while exploring friendship, desperation, ambition, empowerment, and the consequences of crossing moral boundaries.

🎭 Genre: Crime • Drama • Dark Comedy • Thriller

⭐ IMDb: 7.7/10

⏱️ Runtime: Approximately 43 minutes per episode • TV-14

🎥 Creator: Jenna Bans

📺 Seasons: 4 • 50 Episodes

📍 Setting: Suburban Detroit, Michigan.

📺 Where to Watch: Netflix (United States; availability may vary).

source_details.synopsis: Good Girls is an American crime comedy drama television series that follows the lives of three suburban mothers who resort to robbing a supermarket and get involved with a crime boss and the FBI. The series was created by Jenna Bans and aired for four seasons on NBC, from February 26, 2018, to July 22, 2021. It stars Christina Hendricks, Retta, and Mae Whitman as the main characters, along with a supporting cast that includes Reno Wilson, Manny Montana, Lidya Jewett, Isaiah Stannard, and Matthew Lillard. The series was executive-produced by Bans, Dean Parisot, and Jeannine Renshaw, for Universal Television. In June 2021, NBC announced that the show was canceled after four seasons.
